question: Will nodejs.org/dist/index.json list Node.js v26.14.0 or later with a release date on or before Dec 11, 2026?
resolutionCriteria:
Resolution criteria:
- "Yes": Wins if `https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json` contains an entry whose version field is "v26.14.0" or any higher v26.x.x (or any later major) release, and whose date field is on or before "2026-12-11", with that entry first appearing in the feed strictly after 2026-11-24T09:13:13.143Z and confirmed present at or before 2026-12-12T07:59:59.000Z.
- "No": Wins if, at 2026-12-12T07:59:59.000Z, `https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json` contains no entry satisfying the conditions above.

Clarifications:
- The window for a qualifying release is strictly after 2026-11-24T09:13:13.143Z (windowStart) and at or before 2026-12-12T07:59:59.000Z (settlementStartsAt). A release whose date field is on or before 2026-12-11 but whose entry does not appear in the feed by 2026-12-12T07:59:59.000Z does not satisfy "Yes".
- Version comparison follows semantic versioning: v26.14.0 is the minimum qualifying version; any v26 patch or minor release ≥ v26.14.0, or any Node.js major version > 26, also qualifies.
fact: nodejs.org/dist/index.json at 2026-11-26T15:20:04.934Z lists 21 v26.x.x releases; the highest is v26.13.1 dated 2026-11-10. The market's minimum is v26.14.0 with date on or before 2026-12-11. The median gap between recent v26 releases is 7 days; 16.6 days had elapsed since v26.13.1 (2026-11-10) at read time, putting the next v26 release around 2026-11-17 on that cadence.
relevance: Resolution checks this exact JSON feed for a v26.14.0-or-later version with a date on or before 2026-12-11, present by 2026-12-12T07:59:59Z. The cadence arithmetic is computed from the feed itself, not from commentary.
working: Filtered 884 entries to /^v26\.\d+\.\d+$/ (21 matches), sorted by semantic version, highest=v26.13.1, then compared with v26.14.0. Cadence: median gap 7 days over 9 releases; days since last 16.6; overdue 9.6.
